_read_me: TEMPLATE. Copy to jobs/settings.json (gitignored) and rewrite every section for your own search. Until you do, the scrape ranks jobs for the made-up person below: a QA / AI-testing engineer in Lisbon with an EU passport. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored. Every list of words is a list of PHRASES, matched case-insensitively on whole words: "qa" matches "QA Engineer" but not "Qatar"; a * means any letters, so "game design*" matches "Game Designer"; a phrase starting with re: is a raw regular expression (in JSON, write a word boundary as \\b).

you._note: Where you are and where you may legally work. authorized_countries takes country names, or EU / EEA as shorthand. regions are the region words that include you - a posting saying 'EU only' or listing 'Europe' as its hiring region is open to you when the word is here.

location._note: on_site_at_home: 'ok' ranks office jobs where you live as their own tier; 'reject' drops them (for a search whose point is leaving). relocation_targets are places you would move to for an on-site role: list cities, or leave places empty to accept the whole country. accept_country_locks: countries where a 'hires only in X' list still stays on your sheet, penalised rather than dropped. A posting that names a UTC offset further than max_timezone_gap_hours from yours counts as locked.

roles._note: One entry per kind of job you would apply for, best first - the first matching role picks the CV. titles decide whether a posting is this role at all. cv is a variant name from cv/profile.json. cv_rules switch to another variant when the posting looks a certain way. max_level is intern, junior, mid, senior, lead or principal; above it the posting is penalised or, with above_level 'reject', dropped. internships: true, false, or the name of an interest that makes one worth it.
roles.name: ai_qa

_exclude_note: exclude_titles drop a posting when they appear anywhere in its title - other professions, or stacks you do not work in. A role's allow_excluded lets one back in (a 'QA/DevOps Engineer' is still QA). exclude_departments only count at the start of the title: 'Data Analyst, Marketing' is a data job, 'Marketing Manager' is not yours.

interests._note: Themes worth extra points wherever they appear. title_points when the title shows one, text_points when only the description or the company does. A role with the same interest already pays for it and does not collect it twice.
interests.name: AI

_search_note: What to search for on the job boards that need a query (Himalayas). Use the words your target job titles use.

scoring._note: min_score is the bar a posting must clear to reach TODAY_SCRAPING.md. max_per_company stops one employer filling the sheet.

tailoring._note: skills is the whitelist a tailored CV may headline - name -> phrases that mean it in a job description. Leave it empty and the short skill names in your profile.json are used. gaps are things you do NOT have: never put on a CV, only reported so you can prepare. weak skills are real but never enough to headline a keyword block on their own.

llm._note: Optional. Lets `python -m jobs.paste` ask a model to read a whole job description and say apply / consider / skip, then answer follow-up questions. Leave provider empty to stay rules-only. provider: anthropic (key from $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, model defaults to claude-opus-5), openai (key from $OPENAI_API_KEY, set model), or openai-compatible (set base_url and model; api_key_env names the variable holding the key - OpenRouter, Groq, Mistral, or a local Ollama that needs none). The key is never read from this file.
